title: The Diamond Sutra
author: Unknown
description: The Diamond Sutra (Vajracchedika Prajnaparamita Sutra), here in the Project Gutenberg edition titled The Diamond Sutra (Chin-Kang-Ching) or Prajna-Paramita, an early twentieth-century English translation from the Chinese with preface and introduction. One of the most revered texts of Mahayana Buddhism, it records a dialogue at Shravasti between the Buddha and his disciple Subhuti on the perfection of wisdom. The Buddha teaches that a bodhisattva must vow to liberate all beings while holding no notion of self, being, living entity or person; that all phenomena and even the Buddha's teaching are empty of fixed nature, like 'a dream, an illusion, a bubble, a shadow'; and that merit from understanding even four lines of the sutra surpasses immeasurable gifts. Central to Chan and Zen (it famously enlightened Huineng), it is also the text of the oldest dated printed book, the Dunhuang copy of 868 CE.
